# Using the Sample Size Calculator {#sec-calculator-workflow}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Learning objectives"}
- Reproduce a calculation transparently in the application.
- Identify where assumptions and rounding are documented.
:::

## The idea

The [Sample Size Calculator repository](https://github.com/DrNaveen01/sample-size-calculator) contains the R/Shiny code, methods notes, validation documentation and reporting features. Start with the chosen **method and estimand**, not the user interface. Enter probabilities in the units requested by the UI, verify group order, inspect assumptions and examine the numerical substitution before recording a final target.

## When and how to apply it

The application supports several normal-approximation methods and downloadable calculations. It is an adjunct to judgement rather than a substitute. The book may refer to software modules that change between releases: each final worked example should identify the tested app version and date.

## Teaching case 1 — baseline draft

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" title="Clinical scenario / initial worked example"}
Reproduce the single-proportion example $p=0.50$, $d=0.05$, 95% confidence; compare reported complete size, nonresponse inflation convention and the textual report.
:::

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple" title="Common error"}
A screenshot or export from software is not enough methodological justification for a protocol.
:::

## Hands-on exercise

Use the README to run the app locally. Capture inputs, method, assumptions, generic formula, substitution and interpretation.

## Key message

The calculator documents an eligible calculation; it does not decide scientific validity.
